edits.before: Simple historical rules are strong competitors for predicting the largest sampled absolute position before a monitoring horizon ends. The clearest repeated conditional gain occurs for long-history FX regression at the shorter horizon, where same-history comparisons favor regression in both periods. The later gain survives the evaluated calibration wrapper, but unwrapped regression breaches more frequently and its comparison with a shorter-history rolling rule changes direction. The useful gain is therefore specific: long-history short-horizon FX regression beats matched headroom, while its broader ranking depends on the reference.
edits.after: Simple historical rules are strong competitors for predicting the largest sampled absolute position before a monitoring horizon ends. The original long-history FX regression gains against matched headroom survive in the broader backcast on previously examined observations, although score reductions coexist with more breaches. Longer-horizon backcast gains and the daily exception prevent a literal short-horizon or hourly-only interpretation. The controlled simulation also rejects the proposed narrow-regime restriction, while the same-dealer aggregation contrast leaves frequency mixed with measurement and clock changes. The defensible result is reference-sensitive comparative accuracy in these records, rather than a universal mechanism or validated operating-limit rule.
edits.reason: R1–R6: conclusion follows all adverse and qualifying evidence, not only original favorable pattern
